result.title: Efficient Wide-Beam Generative Retrieval with Model-Native Trie Decoding and Shared-Context Attention
result.summary: Generative retrieval (GR) predicts catalog entries as short semantic identifiers (SIDs). Trie-constrained beam search keeps these identifiers valid, but wide beams expose two serving costs: vocabulary-wide score tensors that are mostly discarded, and repeated attention over the same prompt. We present Trie-Head, a model-native output interface that stores the identifier trie as validated GPU tensors. Compared with a Python custom logit processor (CLP), it reduces CPU--GPU coordination and memory traffic by avoiding Python constraint callbacks and vocabulary-wide candidate buffers. It scores compact codebook candidates and streams the full-vocabulary normalizer, preserving the original model's valid-token scores in real arithmetic without retraining. Shared-context attention complements this output path by reusing prompt key/value blocks across beams while preserving their private decode tails. We implement both mechanisms in SGLang and evaluate candidate sourcing for LinkedIn Hiring Assistant and qualification retrieval for the Qualification Retrieval Platform. The combined system improves closed-loop throughput by up to 5.57x over the CLP baseline and up to 2.63x over BF16 FlashRec at a common beam width of 200 on the Qualification Retrieval Platform workload.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向生成式检索的宽 beam 服务效率，提出 Trie-Head：将 SID trie 存为经校验的 GPU 张量实现模型内约束解码，避免 Python 约束回调与全词表候选缓冲，并用 shared-context attention 在 beam 间复用 prompt KV、保留各自私有解码尾，在 SGLang 中实现并报告吞吐提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享上下文 KV + 私有解码尾」的宽 beam 机制，可能为多假设 latent 推理中共享前缀缓存与各假设状态隔离的开销结构提供核查线索，但任务是检索服务优化，与视觉推理无直接关联，迁移价值待判断。
